text:
sam.sales: Hey team, HelixMed POC just pinged asking for a connectivity runbook for Private deployment. They want PrivateLink into our VPC, but need source IP preservation for audit logs and also have strict egress firewall rules. Can we outline what they actually need?

alex.se: Quick summary of ask: 1) PrivateLink (interface endpoints) from customer VPC to Redwood Private endpoint 2) Preserve client/source IP at app-level (they currently rely on x-forwarded-for) 3) Minimal egress ports allowed (only 443 outbound to our management/control plane, maybe 123 for NTP) 4) Clarify cost impacts (data processing/endpoint charges)

maria.neteng: PrivateLink won't preserve original private source IP to our ENIs — traffic comes from the customer's endpoint ENI IPs inside their subnet; on our side we see the endpoint ENI as the source. So if they need true client IP, we usually recommend one of two patterns:
- Path A: Customer front a reverse proxy in their VPC that forwards X-Forwarded-For (TLS passthrough or TLS-terminating with header) to us. We then use XFF for audit logs.
- Path B: Use a transit or peered path where we can preserve src IP (e.g., VPC peering or TGW with route propagation). That requires cross-account peering/TGW attachments and changes to their network ops (not always allowed).

sam.sales: They said peering is disallowed due to security policy, so PrivateLink is the only approved pattern.

alex.se: Ok with PrivateLink only, we should document header propagation approach and include example config for typical app servers to log X-Forwarded-For. Also confirm TLS termination requirements and mutual TLS if they want stronger auth.

chantal.cs: Also call out healthcheck and idle timeout behaviours. HelixMed uses a long-lived gRPC stream for some inference paths — do we support this over PrivateLink?

alex.se: We do support streaming over HTTP/1.1 chunked and HTTP/2/gRPC. Notes: ALB/NLB behaviours differ. For PrivateLink-backed NLB -> target group setup, TCP-level passthrough keeps client IPinfo to the target (again, endpoint ENI IPs). For app-level XFF, gRPC metadata carries it if proxy forwards. For long-lived streams we advise disabling aggressive idle timeouts on their proxy: keepalive / tcp_keepalive settings or HTTP2 ping.

maria.neteng: Firewall ports to allow from their side: outbound to our PrivateLink ENI is just normal VPC traffic. For any management/control connections (if they choose Private with a controller plane over internet) they need outbound 443 to console.redwood.ai and 443 to registry endpoints. If completely private, only PrivateLink endpoints to our service in the region, plus DNS resolution to our service name. We'll need them to allow egress: 443 (HTTPS) and 53 (UDP/TCP) if using AWS VPC DNS and they have custom resolver. NTP (123/UDP) only if they want time sync to our managed layer — otherwise they can keep internal NTP.

sam.sales: They asked about specific SG rules snippet we can share for their security team. Can you paste a minimal example?

alex.se: Sure, here's a minimal SG example for the customer endpoint side (they can adapt):

```
# Customer ENI security group (in their VPC)
Inbound:
  - Type: HTTPS (TCP 443), Source: 10.0.0.0/16  # app clients
Outbound:
  - Type: All traffic to our PrivateLink endpoint ENI (destination: sg-0abcd1234efgh5678)
  - Type: DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to VPC resolver
  - Type: NTP (UDP 123) to their NTP server if required
```

alex.se: And on our side we restrict endpoint SG to only allow inbound from the customer's endpoint security group (we'll ask for the SG ID) and outbound to backend cluster SGs.

maria.neteng: A couple more gotchas to call out:
- MTU: PrivateLink + ENI can reduce path MTU; recommend configuring app clients and proxies for MSS clamping or ensure no oversized packets.
- IP allowlisting: If they want egress allowlisting for things like metrics/telemetry, note that PrivateLink uses endpoint ENIs in our account; we'll provide the endpoint IPs for the region but they can change on redeploy — better to allow by SG rather than static IPs.

chantal.cs: Pricing/POC notes for the deal: HelixMed cares about per-request cost. PrivateLink has per-hour endpoint charges + data processing per GB on endpoint. Also our Private product has committed monthly infra. We need estimated monthly delta in the POC quote.

sam.sales: @maria, can you pull rough PrivateLink cost calc (endpoint hourly + data processing) for us to add into the POC quote? Also add any Redwood side managed egress bandwidth assumptions.

maria.neteng: Will do. Rough calc to share: endpoint-hour ~$0.01-0.02/hr per AZ (depends on aws region), data processing ~$0.01/GB in region (very rough). I'll compute for their expected 5 TB/month.

netops-bot: Automated note: please ensure security questionnaire item S-14 (network architecture) is updated with PrivateLink diagram and SG IDs once provided.

sam.sales: Great. Next steps:
- alex.se to draft a one-page connectivity runbook showing header propagation, minimal SG rules, TLS options, and keepalive hints.
- maria.neteng to provide cost estimate and list of endpoint IPs/SG that will be used in POC region.
- chantal.cs to confirm whether HelixMed will require mTLS or just header-based auditing.

alex.se: Drafted the runbook attached below (short):

"Runbook (summary):
1) Provision an Interface PrivateLink endpoint in customer VPC targeting service:com.redwood.private.region
2) Customer sets endpoint SG to allow outbound to PrivateLink and inbound from app clients
3) Customer deploys a small proxy (envoy/nginx) to terminate TLS and inject X-Forwarded-For header, or do TLS passthrough and rely on ALPN for gRPC with header forwarding if their stack supports it
4) On Redwood side, configure service to read X-Forwarded-For into logs and authz decisions (we will provide config snippet)
5) Test: curl --resolve service.example.internal:443:<endpoint-ip> https://service.example.internal/health with header echo to verify XFF
6) Performance: expect <10ms additional latency inside same AZ; cross-AZ PrivateLink adds ~2-4ms.
7) Cost: Maria will provide numbers.
"

chantal.cs: This is great. Can we also add a short FAQ for their security team about why peering is disallowed and tradeoffs?

alex.se: Added FAQ item: "Why not peering?" -> Peering/TGW preserves src IP but requires broad route acceptance and can expose VPC CIDR ranges across accounts; PrivateLink gives a more narrow, service-focused exposure footprint at the cost of losing raw client source IP (solved via XFF).

sam.sales: Perfect. Let's get the runbook + cost by EOD so I can send the formal POC handoff to HelixMed. :thumbsup:

maria.neteng: Will share numbers by 18:00 PT.

netops-bot: Reminder queued: update security questionnaire S-14 after runbook upload.

sam.sales: Thanks all — I'll stand up a short Zoom with HelixMed for Thursday 9am PT to walk through. I'll post invite.

alex.se: I'll be on the call to walk through the runbook and XFF snippet.
